newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Economists says Australia economy is patchy.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Economists says Australia economy is patchy.

text.p: Australia's economy remains generally weak and might be in need of rejuvenation from another interest rate cut, although some sectors are on the upswing, economists said after analysing data released on Monday.
"The picture remains of a very flat economy that may need further monetary stimulus in the new year," Colonial State Bank senior economist Craig James said.
The Reserve Bank of Australia holds its monthly board meeting on Tuesday but most economists believe the next rate reduction will occur sometime in early 1997.

A Reuters poll of economists put the likelihood of another cut following Tuesday's meeting at only 10 percent, following easings in July and November this year to push the official cash rate down by a total of 100 basis points to 6.5 percent.
Monday's official data showed retail trade rising 1.4 percent in October, which was below expectations, while building approvals jumped 12.8 percent in the same month.

Business inventories data, also released on Monday, was stronger than expected in the third quarter of 1996 and encouraged an upward revision in predictions for September quarter gross domestic product (GDP) data due on Wednesday.
Inventories, which have a direct bearing on the economic growth figures, rose 2.3 percent in the quarter.

Economists surveyed by Reuters now expect GDP to have risen 0.9 percent, and be 3.4 percent higher over the past year. When surveyed last week, economists had been looking for growth of 0.6 percent, and annual growth of 3.1 percent.
While the data appeared to present a mixed bag of economic signals, analysts mostly focussed on retail trade as a guide to where the economy was headed and what the central bank might be about to do.
Westpac senior economist John Peters said the data "reinforces our view that another monetary policy easing is in the pipeline".
